The operator launcher needs subprocess to start a fixed per-user systemd job and the installed trusted CLI. Both calls use structured arguments without a shell. Actual kernel-limit startup guards, pidfd owner-death cancellation, atomic admission and full runtime expiry were tested. This is not an arbitrary-code sandbox.

Executes only /usr/bin/python3 -P -m entrotter_cli with PYTHONPATH replaced by the fixed installed engine/SDK/CLI sources. Safe-path mode rejects the reproduced cwd package spoof; literal scenario/export arguments never pass through a shell. Actual cgroup limits are verified before execution, pidfd monitors the original owner and finally cancels the owned session. Operator-controlled installed source remains trusted.

Executes only /usr/bin/systemd-run with a fixed per-user unit, concrete private EnvironmentFile, fixed resource/time properties and this installed worker script. Structured arguments and disabled systemd environment expansion preserve literal user paths; no shell or credentials in argv. Real duplicate admission preserves the incumbent, and owner SIGTERM/SIGKILL/full 180-second expiry recover. The tiny dispatcher is outside the leaf cgroup but inside the separately verified dedicated VM.
